samir: Nightly eval alert — math_ops prompt set dropped hard on redwood/mistral-3b:fp8-auto-v1. Accuracy went from 98.6% -> 84.3% in 03/19 nightly. Failing at scale, not just flaky. cc @jia @marta
quant-bot: [automated] nightly-eval/1769004800 — model: redwood/mistral-3b:fp8-auto-v1; suite: math_ops; baseline_fp32=98.6; fp8_auto=84.3; delta=-14.3; link: https://ci.internal/reports/1769004800 (metrics + samples)
jia: Can you paste 2-3 concrete failing examples and the float32 baseline outputs? Need to see pattern (arithmetic vs reasoning).
samir: Sure — sample below (cleaned):
```
Prompt: "What is 13 * 7?"
Baseline (float32): "91"
FP8-auto-v1: "13 times 7 equals 101"  <-- wrong numeric token

Prompt: "If you add 47 and 36 what do you get?"
Baseline (float32): "83"
FP8-auto-v1: "seventy nine"  <-- off by 4
```
Seems numeric tokens get garbled, not hallucinations. Also see short tokenization glitches for two-digit numbers.
marta: Noted — we merged a change to the fp8 calibrator on 03/18 (commit 7a2b3f) that switches to global abs_max across the batch for faster stable scales. That was intended to reduce noise but could leak statistics across examples. Link to PR: https://git.internal/rw/quant/pull/224
ryan: Can you repro locally with a deterministic seed and different batch sizes? If it's batch-dependent that points at aggregator bug. I can run a dedicated job:
`rwinf eval-run --model redwood/mistral-3b:fp8-auto-v1 --suite math_ops --seed 42 --batch-size 8 --quant=fp8-auto --out=/tmp/eval_fp8.json`
Also run float32 baseline: `--model redwood/mistral-3b:float32`
ash: (note: added to queue)
ash: (actually I'm ryan — starting job on dedicated-nightly-01)
samir: Reproduced locally. Quick experiment: batch_size=1 -> fp8 matches float32 (98.7%). batch_size=8 -> 84.1%. batch_size=16 -> 82.9%. So failure correlates with batch aggregation.
jia: Hypothesis: global abs_max aggregation causes over-scaling/clipping for some samples producing token distortions for numeric tokens (small integer tokens could get quantized to wrong integer indexes). Can you dump calibration tables per-sample vs global?
marta: I looked at the calibrator code — quant/scale_updater.py — the new path does: `batch_abs = max(abs(tensor))` then `running_max = max(running_max, batch_abs)` across batch. That loses per-sample dynamics. If one example has a spiky token it pushes scale up and reduces resolution for others. For numbers that map to small logit ranges we lose precision.
ryan: Good catch. Quick mitigation: switch to per-sample abs_max during offline calibration: `--quant=fp8-per-sample`. Can we run that as a canary? I'll kick a nightly canary with per-sample mode and also a float32 control.
`rwinf eval-run --model redwood/mistral-3b:fp8-auto-v1 --quant=fp8-per-sample --suite math_ops --seed=42 --batch-size=8 --out=/tmp/fp8_ps.json`
`rwinf eval-run --model redwood/mistral-3b:float32 --suite math_ops --seed=42 --batch-size=8 --out=/tmp/fp32.json`
devops-bot: Job scheduled: job=rw-eval-1769005123 on cluster=dedicated-nightly-01; ETA ~18m; link: https://ci.internal/jobs/1769005123
ash (ryan): Early result: fp8-per-sample -> accuracy 98.5% (matches fp32). So mitigation works. Looks like the global aggregator is the culprit.
samir: Confirmed locally too. So root cause is aggregation across examples during calibration.
marta: I'll open a PR to revert the global-agg change and add a test that runs math_ops with batch sizes 1/8/16 in CI. Will also add a clamp: `scale = max(scale, min_scale)` to avoid tiny-scale underflow. PR incoming: https://git.internal/rw/quant/pull/231
ash (ryan): Please canary the PR to nightly-01 only. Also add a regression test that runs 1000 seeds on the math_ops prompts (cheap, deterministic) and checks numeric-answer accuracy > 98%.
ash (ashley): FYI I saw a small similar blip on the commonsense suite ~2 weeks ago but dismissed (thought noise). I'm going to run a cross-suite sweep once PR lands to ensure no other prompt families are affected. Tagging @security in case customer-facing apps saw wrong numeric answers.
quant-bot: PR 231 created by marta — https://git.internal/rw/quant/pull/231 — status: open; CI: running unit + quant-smoke
marta: Will add a short note in the changelog and a postmortem entry if the PR lands to stable. Quick fix plan: revert global aggregation, add per-sample default for calibration, add clamp and add regression tests. Longer fix: instrument per-token quantization error distributions to detect future drifts.
samir: Good. After canary, if green we'll promote to nightly and invalidate any cached quant profiles that shipped with 03/18 nightly. Also add a one-off job to re-evaluate recent commits and mark affected rollouts.
ryan: I'll handle the canary promotion.
ash (ashley): Thanks all — please ping when PR merges. :thumbsup:
marta: PR merged to nightly branch, canary started (job 1769007890). I'll follow up with exact diff and unit tests.
samir: thanks everyone — big win catching before customer impact. :tada:
